## Amazon RDS: Automated Backups vs. Manual Snapshots

### Automated Backups
- **Enabled by default** when you set a backup retention period greater than 0 (RDS enables them automatically for most engines).
- **How they work:** RDS performs a daily full storage volume snapshot during your configured **backup window**, and continuously captures **transaction logs**.
- **Point-in-time recovery (PITR):** Because of the transaction logs, you can restore to any specific second within your retention period (typically up to the last ~5 minutes).
- **Lifecycle:** They are **managed by RDS** and are automatically deleted when they age out of the retention window or when the DB instance is deleted (unless you take a final snapshot).
- **Storage:** Stored in Amazon S3 managed by AWS; no direct access to the files.

### Manual Snapshots
- **User-initiated** — you create them explicitly (console, CLI, API) whenever you want.
- **How they work:** A full storage-level snapshot of the DB instance at the moment you take it. **No point-in-time recovery** — you can only restore to the exact moment the snapshot was taken.
- **Lifecycle:** They **persist until you explicitly delete them**. They are *not* removed when the DB instance is deleted, which makes them ideal for long-term archival, compliance, or pre-change safety copies.
- **Sharing/copying:** Can be copied across regions and accounts, and shared with other AWS accounts.

### Retention Periods for Automated Backups
- **Configurable range:** **0 to 35 days**.
  - Setting the retention period to **0 disables** automated backups.
  - **Maximum is 35 days** for standard automated backups.
- **Default:** Typically **7 days** when you create an instance via the console (**1 day** when created via the CLI/API/RDS API).
- **Beyond 35 days:** If you need longer retention, use **manual snapshots** (which never expire automatically) or the **AWS Backup** service, which can manage RDS backups with longer, policy-driven retention.

### Quick Comparison

| Aspect | Automated Backups | Manual Snapshots |
|---|---|---|
| Initiated by | RDS (automatically) | You |
| Point-in-time recovery | ✅ Yes | ❌ No (only snapshot time) |
| Retention | 0–35 days (auto-expires) | Until you delete them |
| Deleted with DB instance | ✅ Yes (unless final snapshot) | ❌ No (persist) |
| Best for | Operational recovery, PITR | Long-term archival, compliance, sharing |

**Tip:** A common pattern is to rely on automated backups for day-to-day operational recovery and take manual snapshots before major changes (schema migrations, version upgrades) or for retention beyond 35 days.
